body: Following a redirect changes only the URL, so a same-origin 303 resends the original POST and body instead of issuing a GET. If a GraphQL or rerun request receives this redirect, the destination receives the wrong method and may reject the request. Preserve Fetch's method/body rewriting for 303 responses and POST requests redirected with 301/302, retain the origin check, and add a non-GET redirect regression test.

A legacy link such as `https://github.evil.com./a/b/pull/1` retains `github.evil.com.` in storage, but this call now normalizes its host to `github.evil.com`. The unchanged `_key` comparison consequently returns `was_linked: false` and leaves the link on the list even when its exact stored URL is supplied. Normalize the stored host during the unlink comparison so these older links can actually be removed.

The shared two-worker executor accepts an unbounded queue, but the frontend's 120-second deadline includes queue time. With six simultaneous charts taking 80 seconds each, the last two time out before their model calls start; abandoned calls still consume model capacity, and retries can extend the backlog. Bound queue admission and enforce an end-to-end deadline or cancellation so expired queued requests do not start model calls.

If a chart request is aborted or times out while the RPC acknowledgement is pending, `reply` rejects before a rejection handler is attached. This produces an unhandled rejection and an application fault even though the registry catches the returned author promise, and cancellation cannot settle that promise until the acknowledgement arrives. Await the acknowledgement and reply together so both failures are observed immediately.

Fixed in f27e6e2: a 303, or a 301/302 answering a POST, is now followed with a GET and no body (Content-Type dropped), as fetch does; a 307/308 keeps the method. The same-origin check still runs before every hop. New test: 'follows a POST answered 303 or 302 with a GET and no body, as fetch would; a 307 keeps the POST'.

Fixed in f27e6e2: `_key` now compares the normalised host (and lower-case repository), so a link stored as `github.evil.com.` or `GitHub.com.` before this change is found by unlink, and a new link to the same PR counts as already linked. New test: test_a_legacy_link_stored_with_a_trailing_dot_is_found_by_its_normalised_host.

If this repository has a CLI session but frontend sessions exist only in other repositories, `hermes tern -c` selects an unrelated frontend session and can change into its directory. Search both source groups within the current workspace before searching globally, preserving the documented workspace-first behavior.

Exported launch overrides no longer reach the session policy: for example, `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1 hermes tern` sends no `accept_hooks`, and gateway attach removes that variable before starting the daemon. Preserve truthy `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS`, `HERMES_YOLO_MODE`, and `HERMES_IGNORE_RULES` values alongside the parsed flags when constructing `session.create` options.

Fixed in 1d67856. The RPC now admits at most 8 waiting calls (a 9th fails the call, which the pane counts as one failed attempt). A call that waited in the queue past the pane's deadline answers at once with an error instead of starting a model request, and the model call's timeout is what is left of that deadline.

Fixed in 1d67856. The author now awaits the call and its reply together (`Promise.all`), so an abort or a timeout while the call is still unanswered rejects at once, with no unhandled rejection. A failed call still ends the wait for its reply. New test: 'stops waiting when the request is aborted before the call is answered'.
Fixed in 882ac66. `-c` now searches this workspace for a frontend session, then a CLI session, and only then anywhere.
Fixed in 882ac66. Exported HERMES_YOLO_MODE, HERMES_IGNORE_RULES and HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS (1/true/yes/on) now count as their flags in the `session.create` options.

The newly recorded `viewer.set` requests include inherited Tern variables, but only the PID is normalized here. Running these replays inside a Tern pane therefore produces pane and socket values where all four snapshots expect `tern: {}`, making the tests depend on the terminal running them. Unset the five Tern variables before each replay and restore the environment afterward.

If the user invokes `/new` or selects another session while `viewer.shown` is pending, the startup restore starts a newer switch when the reply arrives and overrides that choice. Capture a switch ticket before the probe and abandon the restore if a subsequent switch invalidated it; cover this with a delayed `shownElsewhere` response.

If the remembered session's directory differs from the pane's launch directory, the launcher has already changed directories and set `HERMES_TERN_SESSION_CWD` before this check. Rejecting restoration here therefore creates the fresh session in the other conversation's directory, whereas the previous launcher-side check kept the original directory. Use `paneCwd` for this fallback while preserving the policy that remote backends choose their own working directory.
Fixed in ab30acf. The golden test clears the five Tern variables before each replay and restores them after, so the snapshots read the same inside a Tern pane.

Fixed in ab30acf. The restore takes a switch ticket before it asks `viewer.shown` and gives up if a switch began meanwhile (also before it resumes). New test: a delayed `viewer.shown`, a /new in between, and no second session or resume.

Fixed in ab30acf. When the restore is refused (another pane shows it, or it no longer resumes), the new session starts in `paneCwd`; with a remote backend (no session folder) it still sends none, so the gateway chooses. New test checks the `session.create` folder.

Titled phase IDs can collide with generated loose-run IDs: a standalone todo `a`, a parent `loose:a`, and its child produce two phases named `loose:a`, even though the todo IDs are unique. `checklistNode` uses those IDs as sibling keys, so the two checklists cannot be identified independently during updates. Namespace titled phase IDs separately, add a regression test for this case, and update the panel snapshot.

Fixed in 9e486e8: titled phases are now keyed `parent:<id>`, runs `loose:<id>`, so no todo id can make two phases share a key. A test covers the case from this comment (`a`, a parent `loose:a` and its child), and the panel golden is updated.

When a model reuses a tool-call ID, `transcript.call()` can return an earlier completed call, and attaching the new card preserves its old result. The immediate poll then marks the new card `stopped`, hiding its controls while the gateway still waits for an answer. Bind only to a current running `manage_connections` call and create a distinct call instance for reused IDs; `Transcript.toolStart()` also needs to stop deduplicating those IDs across turns.

For an MCP server, Connect can install or start a local executable, but this card shows only the app name and state. The gateway supplies a `launch` descriptor with the command and arguments or remote endpoint, which `parseTargets()` drops, so users cannot inspect what they are approving. Preserve and display the scrubbed launch details before offering Connect, or keep MCP approval unavailable until those details can be shown.

The gateway removes a settled operation before returning its tool result, so a status poll can receive 4004 before `tool.complete` when the settling update was missed. This freezes the old rows as `stopped`, and the later authoritative result cannot correct them because both `#tickLive()` and `applyFrame()` reject settled cards. Make this locally inferred settlement provisional and allow the same operation's final result to replace it.

The countdown stays stale while a card is unchanged: `entryNode()` caches the turn by its revision, and equal-sequence status polls neither invalidate that cache nor request a render. Even an unrelated redraw can therefore still show “10 more minutes” two minutes later. Invalidate the card and schedule a render when its displayed minute changes, or use timer-backed text, and test clock advancement through `entryNode()`.

Fixed in 751875a: a request whose `tool_call_id` names a finished call now gets its own row (`connect-<op_id>`) instead of landing on the finished one. Test: "a request naming a finished call of the same id gets a row of its own". I left `Transcript.toolStart()` deduplication alone: Hermes core already renames a reused id before the tool runs (the gateway log says `Model reused tool call id call-connect; renamed the duplicate to call-connect_d2`), so the request and its `tool.start` carry the new id.

Fixed in 751875a: `parseTargets` keeps the gateway's scrubbed `launch` descriptor, and an unresolved MCP row shows it under the name in full ("Runs: …" or "Connects to: …", plus working dir and env names), as Desktop's mcp-setup-tool.tsx does before consent. Test: "an MCP row shows what Connect runs before the user approves it". Checked in the lab against hermes-agent main (`install figma` shows `Connects to: https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`).

Fixed in 751875a: the pane's own `stopped` (from a 4004) is now provisional. When the tool's result arrives for the same `op_id`, it replaces the rows and the settle reason once (links kept). Test: "the tool's result replaces a stop the pane inferred from a 4004".

Fixed in 751875a: the watcher's 2 s poll touches the card when the shown minute changes, so the cached turn node is rebuilt. Both the view and the watcher use one `minutesLeft()`. Test: "the wait redraws as its minutes count down" (advances the clock and renders through `entryNode()`).

A batch can contain the same question text with different choices, but `findIndex` always maps both requests to the first occurrence. The second card then shows “Question 1 of 2” and still labels its final action “Next” instead of “Submit”. Only emit a place when the text matches uniquely, or disambiguate using additional request data; an unknown place is preferable to incorrect progress.

After typing an Other answer in a multi-select and pressing Esc, its new checkbox is checked, but Space or its number key only reopens the input instead of toggling it off. Submitting still includes that text, so deselecting Other requires deleting the draft despite the “toggle” hint. Track its selected state separately from its text and honor that state when submitting.

Fixed in 89e557b. A card whose text matches several questions is told apart by its choices (without the `(Recommended)` suffix). If it still matches more than one, it gets no place. Test: `by its choices when two questions read alike, and none when they still match both`.

Fixed in 89e557b. Other has its own checked state: its number key or space unchecks it and keeps the draft, and an unchecked draft is left out of the answer. Enter now submits a multiple choice on the Other row too. Test: `unchecks a drafted Other in a multiple choice`, and checked live in Tern.
